method: Retrospective design review of portfolio materials: case-study texts, design artefacts and planned interview guides.

segments.extract: The design challenge was to make these game systems feel exciting while keeping everyday conversation familiar.
segments.comment: The core tension of the case: excitement from game systems vs. the familiarity of chat.

segments.extract: Telegram was a reference for that continuity: new features can arrive without making people relearn where conversations live.
segments.comment: A named precedent used to justify a stable layout.

segments.extract: the chat list, navigation and message area form that stable foundation; new characters and events provide the changing content.
segments.comment: Separates the fixed frame from changing content; matches the Home and Chat screens.

segments.extract: Sign-up. 50 gems on joining, enough for five spins.
segments.comment: The onboarding reward is sized to the mechanic (five spins).

segments.extract: The characters belong to one world, connected by friendships, intrigues and investigations.
segments.comment: A shared story world gives a reason to return beyond collecting.

segments.extract: This gives the chat both an immediate use and a longer thread to return to.
segments.code_names: Stated intention; Progress to a goal
segments.comment: Two time horizons: a chat now and a story over time.

segments.extract: Story apps such as Romance Club were a reference for the appeal of getting to know characters over time.
segments.comment: Second named precedent.

segments.extract: character profiles introduce interests in the character’s own voice, while suggested replies offer a starting point when someone does not know what to say.
segments.comment: Two devices lower the cost of a first message; visible on the profile and chat screens.

segments.extract: I connected the interface flow with the currency model so that finding a character, earning gems and trying a banner belonged to the same product logic.
segments.comment: Role spans UX and economy design.

segments.extract: I proposed gacha as a defining part of the concept.
segments.comment: Ownership of the core mechanic.

segments.extract: A subscription would not directly unlock the whole cast: characters would be obtained through pulls, using currency earned through tasks or purchased in the shop.
segments.code_names: Collecting & discovery; Currency & rewards; Spending pressure
segments.comment: Access is tied to pulls; randomness may frustrate people who want one specific character.

segments.extract: character drop rates, a guaranteed five-star after a set number of pulls, and soft pity that increases the odds before that guarantee.
segments.code_names: Transparency of cost & odds; Progress to a goal
segments.comment: The probability model has explicit guarantees.

segments.extract: The banner exposes the odds and the remaining distance to the guarantee, so the next attempt has visible context.
segments.code_names: Transparency of cost & odds; Progress to a goal
segments.comment: Matches the pity bar and rates list on the banner screen.

segments.extract: The Bestie Pass offers a daily supply of gems rather than direct access to every character.
segments.comment: Subscription supplies currency, not characters.

segments.extract: I chose a blue-to-green gradient to give the product an energetic, recognisable accent.
segments.comment: Brand colour decision.

segments.extract: the gradient draws attention to messages, character announcements and the next action without making every element equally loud.

segments.extract: The persistent announcement at the top keeps a new character visible across the experience.

segments.extract: This supports two different intentions: returning to someone you know and looking for someone new.
segments.comment: Return and discovery as two parallel routes.

segments.extract: Character discovery has several entry points: the home banner, the library and the announcement strip.
segments.comment: Three entry points listed; all visible on Home.

segments.extract: I also proposed a prompt to try for a character alongside the profile, on the right, when curiosity about that character is already high.
segments.comment: A pull prompt at the moment of highest interest; a proposal, not shown in the screen.

segments.extract: Purchase offers sit in the gem shop and gacha flow, where the user is already considering currency or a pull.
segments.comment: Offers are kept out of the chat.

segments.extract: The aim was to support monetisation without letting purchase messages dominate the conversation.
segments.comment: Stated limit on monetisation pressure.

segments.extract: My central hypothesis was that the anticipation of meeting a character, followed by an ongoing story, could make that relationship feel more personal.
segments.comment: A hypothesis, not a measured outcome.

segments.extract: The next validation would check whether newcomers understand how characters are obtained, can find a route to earned gems, and move from a first pull into a meaningful chat.

segments.extract: Each entry describes a concrete action, so someone can choose between practising alone, listening to guidance or following a breathing rhythm without first navigating a large catalogue.

World is a triptych I made at the start of Russia’s full-scale war against Ukraine in 2022.
segments.comment: Context of the work.

segments.extract: It reflects my response to the world’s reaction: realisation, a sense of betrayal and the wait for action.
segments.comment: Three feelings across three panels.

segments.extract: The design decisions serve an emotional statement: the portraits, colour fragments and handwritten words work together to communicate the tension of that moment.
segments.comment: Every element serves the statement.

segments.extract: I built the compositions in Procreate using black-and-white stock photographs of people in traditional Ukrainian dress.
segments.comment: Technique and source material.

segments.extract: painted fragments, yellow outlines and handwriting interrupt it with colour and a more immediate, personal voice.
segments.code_names: Recurring motif; Accent colour as signal
segments.comment: Interruptions as the expressive layer.

segments.extract: The repeated visual language holds the three panels together while allowing each composition to stand alone.
segments.comment: Coherence and independence.

segments.extract: Viewed as a group, the portraits and lettering become a continuous wall of images and statements.
segments.comment: Group reading differs from single panels.

segments.extract: My role covered the concept, image selection, collage, colour treatment and handwritten elements.
segments.comment: Scope.

segments.extract: World was shown at PRAY4UKRAINE, a charity exhibition that directs proceeds from sold works to the Armed Forces of Ukraine.
segments.comment: Exhibition context.

segments.extract: The triptych also won a prize in the Fine Art category of the Nezalezhne Slovo (Independent Word) project.
segments.comment: Recognition.

segments.extract: The series shows how I use contrast, repetition and lettering to carry a message across several compositions.
segments.comment: Transferable skill named by the designer.

I create event posters, graphics and T-shirt prints for a community that meets around both technical interests and social activities.
segments.comment: Scope and audience.

segments.extract: The KSI mark was the only fixed identity element at the start.
segments.comment: Minimal brief.

segments.extract: The challenge was to give each event its own character while keeping the association visible.
segments.comment: Variety within a series.

segments.extract: I designed the posters for a busy university corridor, where someone might only glance at the wall while rushing from one class to the next.
segments.comment: Viewing context defines hierarchy.

segments.extract: I chose bright, contrasting colours and large type to help each poster stand out in that brief moment.
segments.code_names: Scale contrast; Accent colour as signal
segments.comment: Attention strategy.

segments.extract: The hierarchy gives the event title a clear first read, followed by the details needed to take part.
segments.comment: Two-step reading order.

segments.extract: The machine learning poster turns the word “model” into a spiral; the grill poster uses a halftone ξ.
segments.comment: Concept per poster.

segments.extract: a composition that catches attention on the way past and rewards a closer look
segments.comment: Two distances of reading.

segments.extract: The concept and colour support a practical invitation: what is happening, when, where and how to take part.
segments.comment: Information the poster must carry.

segments.extract: The originals are in Polish; I prepared the English versions for this portfolio.
segments.comment: Localisation for the portfolio.

segments.extract: For merchandise, I drew on programming, binary code and symbols familiar to KSI members.
segments.comment: Insider codes.

segments.extract: The cobalt tee combines a pixel outline with a Polish manifesto about the community.
segments.comment: Manifesto as artwork.

segments.extract: Both designs went to print.
segments.comment: Produced work.

segments.extract: Each direction starts from something members can recognise—shared events, habits or tools—and translates it into a graphic idea.
segments.comment: Recognisable to members; may be opaque to newcomers.

segments.extract: These are concept explorations, shown separately from the two produced designs.
segments.comment: Status of concepts.

segments.extract: The published posters and two printed tees show how I adapt a limited starting identity to different messages and formats.
